treatment.logline: Absorbed in her phone, Anudi leaves the comfort of the family car and enters the rainy roadside world beside the food three-wheeler.

arc.feeling: A small practical adjustment brings her into the next encounter's geography.

treatment.approach: An everyday transitional drama, not a suspense passage: naturalistic Colombo daylight, restrained performances and simple camera positions. Six essential shots total 24 seconds. Build the change from enclosed rear-seat framing to an open roadside view. The rain changes her practical circumstances rather than her emotional register. Her acknowledgment is a small visible nod, with no invented dialogue. Preserve the scoped continuous-walking intention in the edit: isolate the umbrella opening in an upper-body source, with no legs visible, between walking shots.

treatment.geography: Park the family car at the near curb, officeward travel left to right. Rear passenger door faces the pavement. The food three-wheeler stands farther along that same pavement, between Anudi and the building. Keep all roadside cameras on the street side of her walking axis. The driver remains seated; no additional identifiable people are required.

advice: Preserve smartphone-right, umbrella-left and handbag-left-forearm continuity throughout.
Do not initiate the next scene's attempt to pocket the phone.
The car door is already open at the start of the exit angle; elide its opening rather than combining two hard actions.

moments.what: Anudi rides in the rear seat looking at her smartphone while the driver takes the car through Colombo traffic.
moments.cut_uses: A rear-seat medium single includes the driver ahead and moving street through the windows, establishing travel without a redundant exterior.

moments.what: The car stops; Anudi gets out with all belongings; she acknowledges the seated driver and heads toward the building.
moments.cut_uses: B curbside wide for the stop, C pavement medium-wide for the exit through an already-open door, then D medium for a nod and officeward walk. Each hard action has its own source.

moments.what: Rain begins; Anudi opens her umbrella on her route and passes the food three-wheeler.
moments.feeling: Her hands become occupied as the two story worlds meet.
moments.cut_uses: E upper-body medium isolates the rain onset and umbrella opening, between the departing walk and F held wide of her passage beside the food vehicle. The cut implies the continuous walk requested by the direction, while avoiding a hard action during travel in the generated source.

editor_notes: The six must sources run 24 seconds in total for a 23-second target; they are raw coverage, not a binding assembly. The four-second roadside shots have half-second handles so their three-second block clock fits.
2A-1 establishes cabin travel and phone absorption; 2B-1 establishes the curb stop. 2C-1 covers the exit with the door already open. 2D-1 carries the silent courtesy and start of the walk.

2E-1 isolates the umbrella opening in an upper-body frame; 2F-1 supplies the continuing walk past the food vehicle. Cut from the walk into the cropped opening and back out to the walk to suggest the scoped continuous action without requiring a hard action during travel.

Match phone in right hand, closed then open umbrella in left hand and handbag on left forearm. Match left-to-right screen direction and introduce rain only at the weather turn. Keep the phone in hand for the next scene.
The door opening is elided; do not imply a door closing or vehicle departure that was not captured. The driver's courtesy is a nod, not an invented spoken line.
If desired, speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in and split screen are post-only techniques; these clips are clean sources and none is required by the intended cut.
Avoid mirrors, fast finger work, physical contact and sharply resolved crowds. The open umbrella shot is isolated to make the prop change more reliable.
